source.paraphrase: Function size exceeds the selected source-code limit.

invariants.why: Function size exceeds the selected source-code limit.
invariants.fixHint: Extract a cohesive operation and preserve behavior with relevant tests.
invariants.avoid: Do not compress statements or split a coherent operation arbitrarily.

source.paraphrase: Function parameter count exceeds the selected limit.

invariants.why: Function parameter count exceeds the selected limit.
invariants.fixHint: Review whether the inputs describe a cohesive domain value.
invariants.avoid: Do not hide unrelated inputs in a generic map. Receivers do not count; tuple inputs count each element.

source.paraphrase: Source control-flow nesting exceeds the selected limit.

invariants.why: Source control-flow nesting exceeds the selected limit.
invariants.fixHint: Use an early return or name a cohesive inner operation.
invariants.avoid: Do not hide nesting in macro token trees; this check measures source AST, not expanded code.

source.paraphrase: A wildcard use obscures the owner of an identifier.

invariants.why: A wildcard use obscures the owner of an identifier.
invariants.fixHint: Use named imports, or document a deliberate prelude or DSL exception.
invariants.avoid: Do not copy definitions to avoid an import. Reviewed preludes can remain an explicit exception.

source.paraphrase: A mutable static needs an explicit synchronization and safety policy.

invariants.why: A mutable static needs an explicit synchronization and safety policy.
invariants.fixHint: Prefer a value or a synchronized owner; review FFI and low-level requirements.
invariants.avoid: Do not replace a mutable static with hidden unsafe global storage.

source.work: Rust standard library documentation, macro std::dbg
source.paraphrase: dbg! is a debugging tool; avoid keeping uses of it in version control, other than in tests and similar. Production debug output belongs to facilities such as the log crate's debug! macro.

invariants.why: dbg! writes file, line and value to stderr on every call, so a leftover one leaks values into production output.
invariants.fixHint: Delete the dbg! and keep its inner expression, or replace it with a log or tracing macro at debug level.
invariants.avoid: Do not move the call behind an alias, std::dbg! or a #[cfg(not(test))] block. Tests, benches, examples and #[cfg(test)] modules are not checked.

source.work: Rust standard library documentation, macros std::todo and std::unimplemented
source.paraphrase: todo! indicates unfinished code and conveys an intent to implement it later; unimplemented! makes no such claim. Both panic when reached.

invariants.why: todo! compiles and type-checks, so a path that looks finished panics the first time it runs.
invariants.fixHint: Implement the path, return an error the caller can handle, or use unimplemented! with a message when the operation is deliberately not provided.
invariants.avoid: Do not swap todo! for panic!("todo"), an empty default value or core::todo!.

source.paraphrase: unimplemented!() indicates unfinished or unimplemented code that panics at runtime when reached.

invariants.why: Leaving unimplemented!() in executable production code creates latent panics on unexplored branches.
invariants.fixHint: Complete the implementation or return a Result::Err value that callers can handle.
invariants.avoid: Do not deploy code containing active unimplemented!(), std::unimplemented!() or core::unimplemented!() branches.
